messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: How to determine data loading progress in Shiny?
parts:
It shouldn't show transient error messages before showing the plot, in general--however it will if your reactivePlot function happens to throw an error. This is most common when using reactiveUI and the value is not available yet. You can avoid the error message by checking for the input value not being available and returning NULL from reactivePlot immediately, i.e. if (is.null(input$foo)) return(NULL);

To show progress, Shiny adds the "recalculating" CSS class to any output element that is in progress, you could add some CSS rules for that.

messages.subject: Re: How to determine data loading progress in Shiny?
parts:
Yes, in the ui.R.

There's no possible way to know how much time is left. You can determine the elapsed time in pure JavaScript if you wanted to; whenever that conditionalPanel condition is evaluated, run a function. This function will see if the busy status (presence/absence of shiny-busy CSS class on <html>) has changed since the last time. If it has changed from not-busy to busy, then save the current time. Then once every second or so (using setInterval) calculate the number of seconds since the start time, and update the progress message with that value.

var wasBusy = false;
var elapsedTimer = null;
var startTime = null;
function updateBusy() {
  var isBusy = $('html').hasClass('shiny-busy');
  if (isBusy && !wasBusy) {
    startTime = new Date().getTime();
    elapsedTimer = setInterval(function() {
      var millisElapsed = new Date().getTime() - startTime;
      $('progress').text(Math.round(millisElapsed/1000) + ' seconds have elapsed');
    }, 1000);
  }
  else if (!isBusy && wasBusy) {
    clearInterval(elapsedTimer);
  }
  wasBusy = isBusy;
}

where $('progress') should have progress replaced with the id of the div or whatever that contains the progress message.

Yes, in the ui.R.

There's no possible way to know how much time is left. You can determine the elapsed time in pure JavaScript if you wanted to; whenever that conditionalPanel condition is evaluated, run a function. This function will see if the busy status (presence/absence of shiny-busy CSS class on <html>) has changed since the last time. If it has changed from not-busy to busy, then save the current time. var wasBusy = false;
var elapsedTimer = null;
var startTime = null;
function updateBusy() {
  var isBusy = $('html').hasClass('shiny-busy');
  if (isBusy && !wasBusy) {
    startTime = new Date().getTime();
    elapsedTimer = setInterval(function() {
      var millisElapsed = new Date().getTime() - startTime;
      $('progress').text(Math.round(millisElapsed/1000) + ' seconds have elapsed');
    }, 1000);
  }
  else if (!isBusy && wasBusy) {
    clearInterval(elapsedTimer);
  }
  wasBusy = isBusy;
}

where $('progress') should have progress replaced with the id of the div or whatever that contains the progress message.
